title: Why Mirrors Seem to Flip Left & Right
tags: do mirrors flip left and right
description:
Why do mirrors seem to flip left and right but not top and bottom? You look in the mirror and the writing on your T-shirt looks reversed. Raise your right hand, and the “other you” raises the left. It feels obvious that mirrors swap left and right—but that’s actually a misconception. What’s really happening is far stranger: mirrors flip front to back along the Z-axis, not left to right or up and down.

In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we break down how light and reflection really work. Using simple examples—pens, writing on paper, car rear-view mirrors, and even ambulance signage—we show that mirrors don’t do the flipping. It’s you who rotate or reposition objects before presenting them to the mirror, and the mirror simply reflects photons back to your eyes.

If you’ve searched for “do mirrors flip left and right, mirror image explained, why mirror reverses text, mirror reflection physics, true mirror illusion”, then this video gives you the scientific perspective. We explain the law of reflection, why mirrors create the illusion of reversal, and how “true mirrors” (made with two mirrors at right angles) reveal what your face really looks like.

Mirrors don’t reverse left-right or top-bottom. They reverse in-out. Once you understand this, you’ll never look at your bathroom mirror the same way again. Don’t forget to like, share, comment, and subscribe for more everyday science myth-busting!
